newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Twelve killed in overnight Colombian violence.
newsitem.headline: Twelve killed in overnight Colombian violence.

text.p: At least 12 people were gunned down in violence overnight across Colombia, including seven victims of execution-style killings in the slums that ring the northwest city of Medellin, authorities said on Friday.
The dead also included five soldiers caught in an ambush by leftist rebels near the town of Arauquita on the country's northeast border with Venezuela, military spokesmen said.

Police said the worst bloodshed occurred in Santo Domingo Savio, a poor neighbourhood on the northeast outskirts of Medellin, where unidentified assassins killed six people with single pistol shots fired at point-blank into their heads.

The victims were all men aged between 18 and 28. Police said the fact that at least two of them had police records indicated that the killings may have been the work of a right-wing vigilante waging a campaign of "social cleansing."

In the nearby municipality of Bello, police said leftist Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels killed a man who had recently arrived in the area from the violence-torn, banana-producing area of Uraba near Colombia's border with Panama.
The rebels left a hand-painted sign on their victim that read: "We get here too, Fifth Front of the FARC."
Colombia has the highest murder rate in Latin America with 26,642 killings last year alone, according to the National Police.
The metropolitan area of Medellin, home to just over two million people, had long been considered the most violent city in Colombia and accounted for 5,245 of the country's murders last year.
